scope: Bounded validation driver exposing full native mathematical evidence for supplied synthetic integer label grids; no images, detector, production integration, or performance claim

input_transport.arguments: Exactly one fixture input file path is required; no stdin and no delegated process
input_transport.mode: Binary seekable file; initial size checked before processing and consumed-byte limit checked during reads
input_transport.encoding: ASCII only; NUL, non-ASCII bytes and non-whitespace control bytes are rejected
input_transport.record_separator: LF byte; final nonempty record may omit LF
input_transport.empty_file: Legal zero-request batch, no stdout records, exit 0
input_transport.line_byte_accounting: At most 131072 bytes excluding LF, including every other byte such as optional CR
input_transport.file_byte_accounting: At most 67108864 bytes including every LF and CR
input_transport.record_count: At most 10000 requests; the 10001st bounded line is rejected before parsing or evaluation

input_grammar.labels_order: Exactly width*height label tokens in row-major order: y increasing from 0, within each row x increasing from 0
input_grammar.unsigned_integer: One to 20 ASCII decimal digits, leading zeros allowed; no sign, exponent, decimal point, or nondigit; pre-multiply/add checked against 18446744073709551615
input_grammar.numeric_fields: request_id, width, height and every label use the unsigned_integer lexer before their individual domain checks
input_grammar.dimensions: width and height are each in 1..160; width*height <=25600 is checked by division before multiplication or grid allocation
input_grammar.labels: Each mathematical integer label is in 0..7 or exactly 255; 255 means invalid and original direction labels are preserved
input_grammar.extra_tokens: Fatal EXTRA_TOKEN, even if the complete valid grid precedes them on the same line
input_grammar.validation: The complete counted grid and absence of extra tokens are validated before calling any edge factory
input_grammar.request_ids: May repeat; callers requiring unique response association enforce uniqueness themselves

validation_driver_limits_only.maximum_single_response_bytes_including_: The remaining cumulative stdout budget, at most 67108864
validation_driver_limits_only.gmp_bound_reason: For these grids each occupied-cell count is <=25600, there are at most 16 occupied cells, LCM <=25600^16 and denominator <=16*25600^16; chain arclength <=1414*25600. The 128-digit serialization cap is deliberately looser and checked before GMP decimal conversion.
validation_driver_limits_only.core_boundary: These caps constrain this validation adapter, not the native mathematical API. External process wall/RSS/output guards remain required; logical byte/count bounds do not form an operating-system allocation sandbox.

output_transport.format: Compact ASCII JSON Lines, one complete JSON object per successful request, followed by LF; no spaces are emitted between JSON tokens
output_transport.stdout: Protocol records only; stdout is binary on Windows, each complete record is flushed
output_transport.numeric_domain: All numeric fields are canonical exact base-10 JSON number tokens, including arbitrary-precision GMP integers; no floating point, quoted numeric strings, exponent notation, or double conversion
output_transport.reader_requirement: Use an exact-integer JSON reader, such as Python json.loads; a reader that coerces all JSON numbers through IEEE754 double can lose request IDs or weights
output_transport.booleans: closed and returning use JSON true/false
output_transport.ordering: All vectors preserve their native factory order; no sample, chain, membership, or pixel sequence is truncated or numerically resorted by this driver
output_transport.assembly: Every fragment append checks the remaining cumulative stdout allowance and reserves one byte for final LF before append/allocation. The whole success record is assembled before writing, so output-limit rejection emits no partial success record. The full attempted write is charged before operating-system output, preventing reuse of its budget after a partial I/O failure.
output_transport.io_failure: An operating-system write/flush failure can physically truncate a record; this always causes exit 2
output_transport.error_budget: A fatal JSON error record is attempted only within the remaining stdout budget. If it cannot fit or stdout is unusable, no new complete stdout record is emitted and a fixed bounded stderr diagnostic is attempted.

success_schema.raw_chains: Full Chain array from extract_chains(original_grid), deliberately before thinning
success_schema.raw_samplings: Full ChainSampling array from sample_chain(raw_chain,width), one record per raw_chains entry in that same order, including returning cycles
success_schema.template: Full TemplateEvidence from prepare_template(original_grid), or JSON null if and only if the validated grid thins to no surviving physical pixels and prepare_template rejects the empty whole template

ThinningResult.eligible_labels: Complete height-by-width original integer label array, including every 255
ThinningResult.labels: Complete height-by-width thinned integer label array, including every 255
ThinningResult.round_deletions: Array of two-integer arrays [subiteration1_count,subiteration2_count], including the final [0,0] round

Chain.pixel_ids: Complete canonical full-chain physical-ID sequence; closed chains do not repeat their first ID
Chain.returning: Boolean, preserved for every returning junction cycle

ChainSampling.pixel_ids: Full deduplicated selected physical-ID sequence in original chain order
ChainSampling.arclength: Exact GMP integer JSON number token

SampleOwnership.member_chain_ids: Complete membership sequence, including nonowning chains

WeightedSample.integer_fields: All fields are exact integer JSON number tokens; chain_index is the original canonical full-chain position, label is preserved, and weight is a GMP integer

TemplateEvidence.thinning: Full ThinningResult, repeated without omissions inside the template
TemplateEvidence.chains: Full Chain array after thinning, retaining zero-owned chains
TemplateEvidence.samplings: Full ChainSampling array after thinning, retaining zero-owned chains
TemplateEvidence.ownership: Full SampleOwnership array in physical-ID order
TemplateEvidence.samples: Full WeightedSample array in physical-ID order
TemplateEvidence.cell_counts: Array of exactly 16 exact integers, including unoccupied zero cells
TemplateEvidence.lcm: Exact GMP integer JSON number token
TemplateEvidence.denominator: Exact GMP integer JSON number token

empty_template_semantics: All-invalid and wholly erased grids are legal requests: top-level thinning, raw_chains and raw_samplings remain fully present and template is null. Nonempty thinned graphs that trigger invalid_argument are unexpected factory failures and exit 2. Unexpected allocation, overflow, logic, and other errors are never converted to template:null.

error_schema.request_id: Normalized request ID after successful parsing; fallback 0 before that, for malformed request IDs, or for input/line/request-limit errors before parsing the next record
error_schema.error: One fixed ASCII ERROR_CODE from the tables below

fatal_error_codes_exit_1.INPUT_LIMIT: Initial file size or consumed input exceeds 67108864 bytes
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.INPUT_CHARACTER: NUL, non-ASCII or illegal control byte
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.LINE_LIMIT: A line exceeds 131072 bytes excluding LF
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.INTEGER_TOKEN_LIMIT: Unsigned integer token is empty or longer than 20 bytes
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.UNSIGNED_DECIMAL: Unsigned integer contains a nondigit, including a minus/plus sign
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.CELL_LIMIT: Grid cell count exceeds 25600, checked before multiplication/allocation; the current per-axis caps already imply this bound
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.LABEL_VALUE: Label is outside 0..7 and is not 255
fatal_error_codes_exit_1.OUTPUT_LIMIT: Next complete success record cannot fit the remaining cumulative 67108864-byte stdout budget

fatal_failures_exit_2.CLI: Wrong argument count; fixed bounded usage on stderr and no JSON error record
fatal_failures_exit_2.BINARY_STDOUT: Windows binary stdout setup failed; fixed bounded stderr and no JSON error record
fatal_failures_exit_2.INPUT_IO: Cannot open, seek or read the input file
fatal_failures_exit_2.FACTORY_INVALID_GRID: A factory rejected the independently validated grid other than the expected empty-template rejection
fatal_failures_exit_2.FACTORY_OVERFLOW: Native factory overflow or an exact integer outside the bounded serialization domain
fatal_failures_exit_2.INTERNAL_ERROR: Other unexpected exception, including logic errors

termination: The first fatal record stops processing; earlier complete success records remain and no later request is evaluated. Exit 0 requires EOF and one complete matching success record for every fixture request. Callers must require exit 0, exact record count, all expected top-level keys, and complete recursive evidence equality.
malformed_test_guidance: For generic malformed cases require exit 1, a listed complete JSON error record when budget/I/O permits, no success record for the invalid request and no later responses. Use an isolated single defect when asserting a specific code; multiple defects can encounter different valid rejection checks. Unexpected failures require exit 2 and must never pass an audit.
execution_claim: Source and protocol prepared without compiling or executing the driver; acceptance requires parent-controlled bounded build and independent-oracle audit. No image accuracy or native performance conclusion follows.
